title: Gopichand on Gayatri's Worlds medal: All players are same
indian_angle: Pullela Gopichand, a legendary Indian coach, shares his perspective on his daughter Gayatri's historic World Championships medal.
summary: Coach Pullela Gopichand discusses his approach to coaching, stating he treats all players equally, including his daughter Gayatri, after her World Championships semifinal run.

title: Gopichand shifts focus to Asian Games after Worlds bronze
indian_angle: This story highlights the strategic planning of India's chief coach Pullela Gopichand for the upcoming Asian Games following a historic World Championships performance.
summary: Following Gayatri Gopichand and Treesa Jolly's bronze medal at the World Championships, coach Pulleela Gopichand is now concentrating on preparing Indian shuttlers for the Asian Games.

title: Treesa, Gayatri impress despite World Championships semi-final loss
indian_angle: It celebrates the impressive run of Indian women's doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand to a World Championships bronze medal.
summary: Indian women's doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a bronze medal at the BWF World Championships, taking the first game against the top seeds before their semi-final loss.

title: Treesa-Gayatri bronze ends 15-year women's doubles drought
indian_angle: This article connects Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand's bronze to the historic 2011 medal by Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa, highlighting a renewed tradition for Indian women's doubles.
summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand's bronze medal at the BWF World Championships marks the end of a 15-year drought for Indian women's doubles, echoing the success of Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa in 2011.

title: Satwik-Chirag exit Worlds in quarters due to fitness concerns
indian_angle: It reports on the quarter-final exit of India's top men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, from the World Championships.
summary: India's star men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty were defeated by China's Chang and Liang in the BWF World Championships quarter-finals, citing fitness issues.

title: Treesa-Gayatri stun fourth seeds, secure historic Worlds medal
indian_angle: This highlights the thrilling quarter-final victory of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, which guaranteed India its first women's doubles World Championships medal in 15 years.
summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured India's first women's doubles World Championships medal in 15 years by upsetting Chinese fourth seeds Jia and Zhang in a thrilling quarter-final.
